verdicts.note: The point codex marked is the LOWER sprocket on the green crank-axle post (chain wraps it and runs UP to the platen); the true pinion beside the big brass drive gear is hidden by the rocker fan, so claude's 'occluded' is correct and codex mislabeled the crank-axle sprocket.
Claude's dot sits on the domed hub of the lower crank-axle sprocket (correct object); codex used this same object as 'pinion_center'.
Left brass helical gear seen end-on; claude sits on the swirl/axis center, codex is ~45px left of center.
Claude's dot is dead-on the polished disc gear's projected axis; codex's point lands on ambiguous helical texture above the disc.

The object codex called a cone is the polished disc — a UNIFORM-diameter gear face, not a tapering stack; the visible green cone is the steel cone_pivot_post, so no brass cone gear is clearly resolvable and claude's 'occluded' is correct.

The arm fan is edge-on and foreshortened here; the marked features are overlapping rounded nubs/rivets, so a single arm's tip corner is not resolvable to corner precision — codex's occluded call is more defensible (claude self-rated low).
Same overlapping bundle; two width-corners of one arm tip cannot be separated to ~5px here.
Both attempts agree the wide butt/pivot ends are occluded behind the frame leg.

Positions tie (~6px apart, both slightly inside the true corner). Naming differs: codex 'top_back_right' is SPEC-consistent (back view: image-left = machine-right); claude 'top_back_left' is image-relative.
Claude's POSITION is on the outer corner; codex is ~30px inward. Naming: codex 'top_back_left' is SPEC machine-relative-correct, claude 'top_back_right' is image-relative.

Claude's Y is the true BOTTOM outer corner of the green slab; codex's Y is ~185px too high (top of slab where the leg meets it). Naming: codex 'base_back_right' is SPEC machine-relative-correct, claude 'base_back_left' is image-relative.

Claude's Y is the true bottom outer corner (dot dead-on); codex's Y is ~180px too high (top of slab). Naming: codex 'base_back_left' is SPEC machine-relative-correct, claude 'base_back_right' is image-relative.

summary: Claude was clearly more accurate on this image: better point placement (cylinder_gear_1, the correct cone-vs-cylinder identity on the polished disc, and the true BOTTOM outer corners of the base slab) and correct object identity throughout (polished disc = cylinder gear not cone; base sprocket = crank-axle sprocket with the pinion correctly called occluded). Codex's one systematic win is naming: it used the SPEC-required machine-relative left/right on the analyzer corners, whereas claude labeled them image-relative (a documented but spec-inconsistent choice). Codex's systematic errors: it marked the base corners ~180px too high (at the top of the slab, not the bottom outer corner), misidentified the crank-axle sprocket as the pinion and the cylinder gear as a cone, and placed cylinder_gear_2 on ambiguous texture.
